verdicts.quote: If any problem is found in the file, no user from the file is created, and the user list is exactly as before. If there is no problem, every row's user is created.
the admin sees one entry per problem row (more if a row has several problems), each containing the line number and a description of the problem

A row whose address already belongs to a user is reported as a problem on its line saying the user already exists. / every row after the first is reported as a problem on its line, saying the address repeats
Every user created by an import has no admin rights, whatever the file contains; the file has no way to grant them.
A signed-in user without admin rights who sends an upload is refused with a message that they lack permission
verdicts.missing: Whether import is a distinct permission from creating a single user, or simply implied by whoever can create users.

verdicts.quote: The first line of the file names the columns. / If the header lacks `email` or `name`, the admin sees a message naming each missing column / A file with extra columns is accepted
A value in double quotes may contain commas, line breaks and a doubled `""` / LF and ... CRLF create the same users / with or without a leading byte-order mark, is read correctly
If any problem is found in the file, no user from the file is created ... An imported user gets the same defaults, the same notifications or invitations
verdicts.missing: Whether invitations/notifications are held until the whole file commits, so none go out for rows when a later row (or a concurrent race, C-37) fails.

verdicts.quote: a file with 1,001 is refused with a message that states the limit of 1,000, and nothing is created / one of 1,048,577 bytes is refused with a message that states the limit
An empty file, or one with only a header line (and blank lines), is refused with a message saying there are no users to import
verdicts.missing: The single-row file case is not stated.

verdicts.quote: They see that nothing was created and that each row's address already belongs to a user. No user is duplicated or changed.
From submit to seeing the result, a valid 1,000-row file takes at most 60 seconds
verdicts.missing: Whether processing is synchronous or in the background, and how the admin learns of completion if backgrounded.

verdicts.quote: An imported user gets the same defaults, the same notifications or invitations ... as a user an admin creates individually
verdicts.missing: Whether up to 1,000 invitations go out at once and any pacing or throttling of them.

verdicts.quote: An imported user gets the same defaults, the same notifications or invitations, and the same way of first signing in as a user an admin creates individually, and can sign in by that way.
with partial creation a corrected file cannot be uploaded again ... They correct the file and submit it again
verdicts.missing: Whether a running import can be cancelled; retry-only-failed-rows is made moot by all-or-nothing but cancellation is undecided.

verdicts.quote: From submit to seeing the result, a valid 1,000-row file takes at most 60 seconds on an ordinary deployment.
verdicts.missing: Whether and how progress is shown while the import runs.

verdicts.quote: Creating one user by hand, editing a user and viewing the list behave as they did before / every user who existed before it has the same name, email, rights and state as before.
one with 255 is reported as a problem on its line naming the email field / one with 101 is reported as a problem on its line, naming the name field
verdicts.missing: Handling of values that begin with formula characters (=, +, -, @) that could execute when output is opened in a spreadsheet.
